subject: ACME POC: integration & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC: post-call recap & next steps

Thanks again for taking the call this morning - great to meet you and Priya. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the 3-week POC we discussed: 

TL;DR: Redwood will provide a scoped POC with a seeded trial account, sample prompts, and an integration checklist. Goal is to validate latency (95th <= 400ms), cost-per-query under target, and answer quality on the ACME customer-support dataset.

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 400ms for single-turn queries (50-200 tokens)
- Accuracy/quality: >= 85% of sampled responses meet ACME scoring rubric (attached template)
- Cost: < $0.02 per query at target traffic profile
- Integration: SDK-based streaming integration working end-to-end in staging

Evaluation plan:
1) Week 0 (this week): share integration checklist and eval metrics template (attached).
2) Week 1: engineering integrates Redwood JS SDK, routes basic query + streaming to staging. Redwood SE (Dev) to support live pairing session.
3) Week 2: run evaluation harness against 2000 queries, gather quality and latency metrics.
4) Week 3: review results, iterate on prompts/quantization profile, and finalize recommendation.

Roles/owners:
- ACME: Jordan (product) + Priya (SRE) - provide test dataset and staging access
- Redwood: Marissa (project lead), Dev (SE / integration), Rishi (sales lead)

Immediate asks for ACME:
1) Share a small staging dataset (200-500 examples) and a service account or temporary staging credentials.
2) Confirm an engineering contact and 2-hour window for a pairing session next week.

Attachments:
- redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (integration steps, sample code, env variables)
- acme-eval-metrics-template.csv (scoring rubric and metric collection)

Proposed pairing slots (PST): Tue 6/22 10-12, Wed 6/23 14-16, Fri 6/25 09-11. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Jordan - adding the PII leakage check as a hard stop (good catch). Updated plan below with a short integration checklist to guide the pairing session. Dev, can you confirm the rough runbook you'll show?

Quick integration checklist (to cover in pairing):
- Environment: staging account + API key / service account; whitelisted IPs or VPC egress rules for Redwood endpoints
- SDK: Install @redwoodai/sdk (Node) or python-redwood; sample init code
  - Node example: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' })
- API routes to exercise:
  - POST /v1/generate (single-turn)
  - POST /v1/stream (server-sent events / websocket) for live agent flows
  - POST /v1/tools/call (tool-calling stub) - for external retrieval calls (e.g., knowledge base)
- Streaming details: show how to consume SSE chunks, handle reconnects, and integrate KV-cache where helpful
- Prompts/tool-calling: brief demo of function/tool schema and expected structured JSON outputs
- Metrics: demonstrate how to export latency (p50/p95), token counts, and sample responses to the eval template

Pairing session goal: get a minimal working integration in staging (Node or Python) with streaming enabled, then run a short 200-query smoke test. Dev, propose 45-60 minutes for the walkthrough + 30 minutes for smoke test.

Next steps:
- ACME: share S3 bucket access + point of contact (Priya confirmed) by Mon EOD
- Redwood: Dev to run pairing on Wed 6/23 14:00 PST; we'll send calendar invite.
- All: confirm any required network allowlists and expected test traffic profile.

Thanks - looking forward to Wed.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ACME POC: integration pairing prep

Hi all - looking forward to the pairing on Wed. A couple of practical notes so we can be efficient: 

1) Quick runbook I'll follow (45-60m):
- 5m: setup and confirm env vars (RW_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION)
- 10m: SDK init + single-turn POST /v1/generate (Node example)
- 15m: streaming demo with /v1/stream (SSE) and reconnect logic + demo of token-level latency reporting
- 10m: tool-calling demo (/v1/tools/call) showing structured function outputs and simple KB retrieval flow
- 10m: smoke test: run 200 queries from ACME sample and show metrics aggregation

2) Code snippets (to save time):
- Node init: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
- Streaming consumption (SSE): client.stream('/v1/stream', { prompt }) -> event.on('data', chunk => ...)
- Tool call stub: POST /v1/tools/call { tool: 'kb-lookup', input: { id: '1234' } } -> returns { content: '...', metadata: {...} }

3) Network: if you're on a private VPC, please confirm the egress IPs or provide a host allowlist for redwood-prod.us-west-2 (we can provision a dedicated endpoint if needed).

I'll attach the minimal sample code to the calendar invite. See you Wed.

-Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
